title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Dubious Buys Raise Alarm Over Local Control of Opioid Cash
summary: Much of the questionable opioid settlement spending in 2025 occurred at the county and city level, where decision-makers often have no background in addiction policy.

title: Opioid Settlement Cash and Homelessness: It’s Not Always Clear How Addiction Fits In
summary: State and local governments are using some of their opioid settlement dollars for initiatives to curb homelessness. The spending raises concerns that those investments don’t always focus on addiction, as many believe the money is meant to.

title: Nebraska Rushed Medicaid Work Rules. Then a Cancer Patient Was Told He’d Lost Coverage.
summary: Nebraska budgeted $8.2 million for contractors to comply with Medicaid changes under President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Health clinics and organizations advocating for poor and working-class Nebraskans say the rollout of Medicaid work requirements has been rife with problems.

title: When a Gun Owner Shows Early Signs of Dementia
summary: Public health experts are finding ways to encourage firearm safety practices for older adults who own guns, especially when there are indications of cognitive decline.

title: The Ultimate Adulting Task: Signing Up for Health Insurance
summary: Buying health insurance can be overwhelming, but there are people who can help you figure it out — free of charge. HealthQ sits in as one 22-year-old speaks with an “independent assister.”

title: Our Reporters Discuss Healthcare Costs — And What Changes the Midterms May Portend
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national and local media in recent weeks to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.

title: Texas Democrats Swept Statewide Races. Now Comes the Hard Part of Solving Healthcare Angst.
summary: The blue wave in the state on Nov. 3 now runs headlong into the reality of Texas politics and a compressed legislative calendar.

title: Healthcare Cuts Fuel Democrats’ Election Blowout
summary: Climbing healthcare costs drove a blue wave this election season. Julie Rovner, KFF Health News' chief Washington correspondent, breaks down the midterms and how the results could shape future healthcare debates.

title: Midterm Wave Sets a Course for ‘Medicare for All’ Fight
summary: Voter frustration with healthcare costs helped fuel the Democrats’ midterm takeover of Congress. But Democratic control doesn’t mean “Medicare for All” will follow, as some hoped.
